title: Getting started
text: Install Vantly, add the return portal to your store, and run a test return. Vantly Returns adds a self-serve return portal to your store and handles each return from request to refund, store credit, or exchange. Setup takes about 15 minutes. 1. Install and open the app After you install Vantly Returns, open it from Apps in your Shopify admin. The Returns page shows a short setup checklist until you finish it. 2. Review your default settings Go to Settings . These are your default terms for every product: the return window, which options customers get (refund, store credit, exchange), fees, and return reasons. Products that need different terms get their own rules later. 3. Add the return portal to your store Your portal already works at yourstore.com/apps/returns . To link to it from your theme: In Shopify, go to Online Store › Themes › Customize . Open the page where the link should go (for example a Returns page or the footer), click Add block , and choose Start a return . Click Save . You can also add the portal link to your navigation menu or your order emails. 4. Make a test return Place a test order, mark it fulfilled, then open your portal and start a return with the order number and email. The return appears in Vantly under Returns , where you can approve it and try the rest of the flow. Next steps Brand your return portal Offer exchanges before refunds Connect return labels

title: The return portal
text: Templates, colors, logo, text, and your return policy. The return portal is where customers start a return: they find their order, choose items and reasons, then pick how they'd like to be paid back. Go to Return portal in Vantly. The page has two tabs: Look for the design and Text for the wording. Choose a template Side by side (the default): built for big screens. What the customer is returning sits on the left and the next step on the right, with no scrolling. On phones it becomes one column. Classic : one bold, focused column with a floating bar, made for scrolling on every screen. Customers can go back a step at any time, and their picks stay filled in. A different choice for each item When a customer returns 2 or more items, they choose what they'd like for each one, one item at a time ("Item 1 of 3"), then see Review your choices with the total. One item can be a refund and another an exchange. Finished items get a check in the list, and customers can click one to change it. (Items from a bundle get one choice for the whole return.) Each different choice becomes its own return in Vantly, linked together. They go back in one box with one label, and the return shipping fee is charged once. See Reviewing returns . Review before submitting After choosing how they're paid back, customers see a summary (what's going back, what they get, and the totals) and press Confirm . It's on by default. To create returns straight away instead, turn off Let customers review before submitting in Settings › Return options . Match your brand On the Look tab, upload your logo and choose its position (left, center, or right). Vantly warns you if the logo is too small to look sharp. Then set your colors, corner style, and font. Change the wording On the Text tab, every piece of text in the portal can be changed, grouped by step: headings, buttons, hints, and confirmation messages. The preview updates as you type, and Open return portal lets you walk through it like a customer. Show your return policy Paste your policy into Return policy and it appears on the first page of the portal. Where customers find it The portal lives at yourstore.com/apps/returns . Add the Start a return block to your theme (see Getting started ) or link it from your menu.

title: Return rules
text: Give products their own window, options, fees, and return reasons. Your default settings cover every product. Rules change the terms for the products they match, like a longer window for snowboards or final sale for clearance items. How rules are checked Rules are checked from the top of the list, and each item follows the first rule that matches it . Anything no rule matches uses your default settings, which are always the last row. Drag a rule by its ⋮⋮ handle to change the order, and put narrow rules (like final sale) above broad ones. Create a rule Go to Rules › Create rule . Applies to : the product (tag, collection, type, vendor, SKU, price, or where it shipped from), the order (tag, discount code, total, date, shipping country, whether it has Vantly package protection, or whether it contains a SKU), the customer (tag, past returns, order count), or the return itself (item condition, reason, chosen outcome, return value). Match any or all of them. Returns : returnable or final sale, the return window, and whether it counts from delivery or shipment. Return options : which of refund, store credit, exchange, and replacement customers can choose. These replace your default options for the items the rule matches. Fees and bonus : restocking fee, return shipping fee, and bonus credit. Leave a field blank to use your default. Return reasons : a reason list just for these products (for example, boots: Too tight, Too loose, Wrong flex). Drag reasons to reorder them, and turn on Photo required for any reason that needs one. Extras : require a photo, approve automatically, let the customer keep the item (always, or only the first time), show a message, waive fees, ask the customer to agree to a statement, tag the customer when approved, or send the items to a return destination . Review and order : flag returns for review, use the rule only once per customer, or let rules below also apply. Different terms for opened items Make two rules, one with the condition Item condition is Opened and one with Item condition is Unopened , and give each its own options and fees. The portal then asks customers whether each item was opened. (Older rules may still show a When opened section; it keeps working.) Test before going live Test on an order shows exactly which rules apply to a real order and why.

title: Exchanges and store credit
text: Keep more sales with exchanges, similar products, and bonus credit. Every exchange or store credit is a sale you keep. Vantly helps customers choose them over a refund, without making refunds hard to find. What customers can exchange for When a customer chooses an exchange, they see other sizes and colors of the same product first, then similar products under "You might also like". If their reason is "too small" or "too big", the portal suggests one size up or down. In Settings › Exchanges , choose where similar products come from: the same product type, collection, vendor, or tag. When the new item ships In Settings › Exchanges , choose Send exchanges : after the returned item arrives, or as soon as the return is approved. If the new item is out of stock, Vantly gives store credit or a refund instead (your choice). Encourage exchanges and store credit In Settings › Return options , choose how the portal presents the options: Gently (recommended): exchange and credit first, with a short perk line; refunds show their timing. Exchange first : the exchange up front, with other options one tap away. Neutral : every option shown the same way. You can also add a bonus (for example 10% extra) to store credit or exchanges. Price differences Choose how exchanges are priced: Free swap : exchanges are always free. Only items that cost the same or less are offered. Customer pays the difference : the customer keeps their original discount. If the new item costs more, they get a Shopify invoice for the difference, and the exchange ships once it's paid. The return page shows whether it's paid, and you can resend the invoice or copy the payment link. Vantly sends one reminder after 2 days. If the new item costs less, choose whether the rest becomes store credit, a refund, or nothing. Staff can also change the price of any exchange on the return page before its order is created.

title: Reviewing returns
text: Approve, reject single items, adjust values, and complete returns. New returns appear on the Returns page. Open one to review it. Work on many returns at once On the Returns page, tick the returns you want, then choose Approve , Mark received , or Complete (up to 50 at a time). Vantly asks you to confirm, and tells you about any return it couldn't change. Approve or reject Approve return accepts it in Shopify and emails the customer the next steps. Reject closes it and tells the customer why. To accept only some items, switch those items to Reject in the Items list and give a reason. The button then reads, for example, Approve 1 of 2 items . Adjust an item's value Click the pencil next to an item's price to deduct or add an amount (for example, a missing part or a goodwill credit). The reason is saved in the return's history; the customer doesn't see it. Receive and complete When the package arrives, mark it received , choose whether to restock each item, then complete the return to issue the refund, store credit, or exchange order. Green returns When a rule lets the customer keep the item, there's nothing to ship back. The customer gets a "You can keep it" email and the return goes straight to payout. Linked returns (different choices per item) When a customer picks, say, a refund for one item and an exchange for another, you get one return per choice. Each one shows a banner, The customer chose something different for other items , with links to the others. Approve and process each one on its own. They share one box and one label, so marking one received marks the others received too. The customer gets one email per step for the whole box (requested, approved, label, received); refund, store credit, and exchange emails go out per return. If the exchange costs more than the item it replaces, money from the refund or credit returns in the same box pays toward it first. Create a return for a customer Customer called or emailed? Click Create return on the Returns page and find the order. It works like the portal, in three steps: Items : click Add details on each item the customer is sending back. Finished items show a ✓ and their choice; click Edit to change one. One screen per item : quantity, reason (or Other (type a reason) ), condition, and What the customer gets : exchange (another size or color, or something else), store credit, or refund. Choose Full value , Set an amount ($) , or Set a percentage (%) , and add an optional note and photos (for example, photos the customer emailed you). Review : check the items and value, then choose Customer keeps the items , Waive all fees , Flag this return , Needs review , and Email the customer . Click Submit . It's approved right away unless you turn on Needs review . Items your rules block can still be added; it's noted on the return as an exception. Different choices for different items become linked returns, one per choice. Restock as a different product In Settings › Restock as , map a product to another one, for example an opened board back into stock as "Used". Choose whether the mapping applies always, only to opened items, or only to unopened ones. You can upload the mappings as a spreadsheet. Return destinations In Settings › Return destinations , add other addresses, like a supplier or a second warehouse. A rule's Where these items go back to sends matching items there, and labels are made out to that address. If a return mixes items for different places, the customer gets one return per destination. Turn off Count these items back into my inventory for drop-ship suppliers. Bundles Bundles sold as one product can be returned by their individual items. Set them up in Settings › Bundles . The refund for each item is what the customer paid for the bundle, split by each item's current store price.

title: Return labels
text: Buy return labels with ShipStation, EasyPost, or Shippo, automatically or by hand. Vantly can buy return labels with your own carrier accounts and rates, then email them to the customer. Which carriers? Vantly connects to carriers through ShipStation, EasyPost, or Shippo , not one carrier at a time. Connect one and you can use USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL , and any other carrier in that account: ShipStation : the carriers you've connected in ShipStation, at your ShipStation rates. EasyPost : EasyPost's discounted USPS, UPS, and FedEx rates, or your own carrier accounts added in EasyPost. Shippo : Shippo's discounted USPS, UPS, FedEx, and DHL rates, or your own carrier accounts added in Shippo. Don't use any of them? You can still add a label by hand on any return (paste a tracking number and label link). Connect an account Go to Integrations and open ShipStation , EasyPost , or Shippo . Paste your API key; Vantly checks it right away and stores it encrypted. It then lists the carriers connected to that account. Test keys work too, for free test labels. International returns For cross-border returns, ShipStation and EasyPost labels include returned-goods customs information automatically. Label rules When buying a label, choose : cheapest, fastest, or best value. Maximum label price : never pay more than this. Only use some carriers and services : tick the carriers or single services you want. Buy a label automatically when a return is approved . Default package : weight is used when products don't have their own. Box size is optional (some carriers price by size). Buy or add a label by hand On a return, you can compare rates and buy a label, or add a label you already have (tracking number and link). Unused labels can be voided for a refund from the carrier.

title: Package protection
text: Offer protection in the cart and keep 100% of the fee. Package protection lets customers add coverage for lost, stolen, or damaged orders. You set the price, you keep the whole fee, and you handle claims your way. Turn it on In Vantly, go to Protection , turn on Offer package protection , set your pricing, and click Save . Vantly creates a hidden Package Protection product with a price for each step. In Shopify, go to Online Store › Themes › Customize › App embeds , turn on Package protection , and save. Pricing Protection is a percentage of the cart, kept between a minimum and maximum and rounded to your price steps (for example $0.50). The widget Choose a toggle card or a Checkout+ button with a "checkout without" link. Change the text, color, and icon, and fill the info popup with your own features and links. The preview shows it on a sample cart, on desktop and on a phone. In checkout (Shopify Plus) Stores on Shopify Plus can also show the switch in checkout: go to Settings › Checkout › Customize , click Add app block , and choose Vantly's protection block.

title: Emails
text: Customize every customer email and send from your own domain. Vantly emails your customer at each step: request received, approved, label, reminder, received, refund or credit, exchange sent, declined, and "You can keep it" for green returns. Change the text and design Go to Emails . Turn each email on or off, and open one to edit its subject and text. Design sets your logo, colors, button style, and footer for all of them. Previews show desktop and phone. Send from your own domain In Emails › Sender and domain , add your domain (for example returns@yourstore.com ). Vantly shows the DNS records to add at your domain provider and checks them for you, including DMARC. Use Klaviyo instead If you connect Klaviyo , you can let your Klaviyo flows send these emails. Vantly then sends the events and stays quiet.

title: Integrations
text: Labels, ShipBob, Katana, Klaviyo, Omnisend, Brevo, Slack, and webhooks. Go to Integrations to connect the tools you already use. Each one has its own page, and keys are stored encrypted. ShipStation, EasyPost, and Shippo Buy return labels with your carrier accounts. See Return labels . ShipBob If ShipBob runs your warehouse, Vantly creates each approved return in ShipBob (with the tracking number when there's a label) and marks the return received when the warehouse gets it. Paste a ShipBob personal access token (in ShipBob: Integrations › API Tokens › Generate New Token ), choose the fulfillment center that receives returns, and choose what ShipBob does with returned items: ShipBob's default, restock, quarantine, or dispose. Items the customer keeps, and items going to a return destination , aren't sent to ShipBob. Katana If Katana manages your stock, Vantly restocks returned items in Katana (matched by SKU) so its numbers stay right. Choose the Katana location, and whether to restock in Katana only, Shopify only, or both. If Katana syncs stock to Shopify, choose Katana only. Klaviyo Paste a Klaviyo private API key with Accounts: Read, Events: Write, and Profiles: Write. Vantly sends an event for each return moment (for example Vantly Return Requested or Vantly Return Refunded ) with the order, items, reasons, amount, and tracking. Build flows and segments on them. Add the flow filter NotifyCustomer is true so staff choices not to email the customer are respected. Omnisend and Brevo Paste your API key and Vantly sends the same return events to Omnisend or Brevo. Under Who emails your customers about returns? , choose Vantly or your email platform; if you choose the platform, Vantly's own customer emails stay off. Send a test event to confirm the key works. Slack Post returns to a channel, like #returns. Create an incoming webhook in Slack, paste the link (it starts with https://hooks.slack.com/ ), and choose what to post: new returns, only flagged returns, or new returns and every update. Each message shows the order, customer, outcome, amount, and items with reasons, plus a button that opens the return in Vantly. Webhooks Send return updates to any system, like a 3PL or ERP. Add an https endpoint and Vantly POSTs JSON to it every time a return changes (for example return.label_created ). Each request is signed with your signing secret in the X-Vantly-Signature header. Coming soon Gorgias (see a customer's returns next to their tickets) and Shopify Flow.

title: Team and permissions
text: Invite your team and choose what each person can do. Until you add someone, everyone on your Shopify staff who opens Vantly is an Admin. To give people different access, go to Settings › Users and roles . Roles Role What they can do Admin Everything, including users, settings, branding, and package protection. Manager All return work, including refunds, exchanges, and price changes, plus rules and bundles. Agent Review returns: approve, reject, notes, labels, and create returns. Can't issue money or change prices. Viewer Can look at returns and analytics, but can't change anything. The store owner is always an Admin. Invite someone Add their email, an optional name, and a role. Tick Email them a link to the app to send them a way in. You can change someone's role or remove them at any time. Everyone else Staff who aren't on the list sets the role for any other Shopify staff member who opens the app, or turns their access off. Who did what Every change on a return is saved in its history with the staff member's name.

title: Plans and billing
text: Plans, return limits, trials, and changing plans. Every plan includes every feature and unlimited staff. Plans differ only by returns per month. Plan Price Returns a month Free $0 20 Starter $29/month or $290/year 150 Growth $79/month or $790/year 500 Pro $199/month or $1,990/year Unlimited Paid plans start with a 14-day free trial. Billing goes through your Shopify invoice. You always keep 100% of package protection fees. If you go over Returns never stop. You'll see a notice in the app and a suggested plan that fits. Change your plan Go to Settings › Plan and billing and click Change plan .

title: Does it create real Shopify returns?
text: Yes. Each return is created in Shopify, so refunds, restocking, and reports stay in your Shopify admin.

title: Can I connect USPS, UPS, FedEx, or DHL directly?
text: Vantly connects to carriers through ShipStation, EasyPost, or Shippo. Connect one and you can use USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, and the other carriers in that account, at your own rates (or EasyPost's and Shippo's discounted rates). No shipping account? You can still add a label by hand on any return.

title: Do customers need an account?
text: No. They find their order with the order number and email.

title: Can I create a return for a customer myself?
text: Yes. Click Create return on the Returns page, find the order, and add details for each item: reason, what the customer gets, and the amount (full value, a set amount, or a percentage). It's approved right away unless you turn on Needs review, and you can make exceptions to your rules.

title: Can a customer get a refund for one item and an exchange for another?
text: Yes. With 2 or more items, the portal asks what they'd like for each item, one at a time. Each choice becomes its own linked return in Vantly, shipped back in one box with one label, and the return shipping fee is charged once.

title: Can I approve or complete lots of returns at once?
text: Yes. Tick returns on the Returns page and choose Approve, Mark received, or Complete, up to 50 at a time.

title: Can I give my team limited access?
text: Yes. In Settings › Users and roles, give each person a role: Admin, Manager, Agent, or Viewer. Agents can review returns but can't issue money.

title: Can some returns go to a supplier or another warehouse?
text: Yes. Add the address in Settings › Return destinations, then use a rule to send matching items there. Labels are made out to that address.

title: Does it work with ShipBob?
text: Yes. Approved returns are created in ShipBob, and Vantly marks them received when the warehouse gets them.

title: Can my email platform send the return emails?
text: Yes, with Klaviyo, Omnisend, or Brevo. Vantly sends an event for each return step, and you choose whether Vantly or your platform emails the customer.

title: Can I get return alerts in Slack?
text: Yes. Connect Slack under Integrations and choose new returns, flagged returns only, or every update.

title: Does it work with my theme?
text: Yes. The portal and the protection widget are built to fit any theme. The widget's colors and text are yours.

title: What happens if I go over my plan's returns?
text: Nothing stops. You'll see a notice with the plan that fits.

title: Who keeps the package protection fee?
text: You do, all of it. Vantly doesn't take a share.

title: What happens to my data if I uninstall?
text: All of your store's data is deleted after Shopify's deletion request. See the privacy policy.

title: How Vantly Cancellations works
text: The cancel portal, step by step, from the customer's side and yours. Vantly Cancellations gives your customers a self-serve page to cancel an order before it ships. Before they confirm, they tell you why and see an offer made for that reason. They can always still cancel. What the customer sees Find order. They enter their order number and email. No account needed. Items and reason. Every item is selected. They untick anything they want to keep, then pick a reason for what they're cancelling. Follow-up questions open under the reason when you've set them up. Review. They see the offer you set for that reason, like a product that solves the problem, a discount, or a size swap. Two buttons: Keep my order or Cancel anyway , with the refund amount shown. Done. A clear confirmation: what was cancelled, what still ships, and when the refund arrives. What happens behind the scenes As soon as a customer starts, the order is put on a fulfillment hold , so your warehouse doesn't ship it mid-decision. Rules decide if the cancel goes through right away, waits for your approval, or isn't allowed. If they keep the order, the hold is released and the order ships. Anything they added from an offer goes on the same order. If they cancel, the items are refunded and restocked, and the order is tagged vantly-cancelled . Where customers find it The portal lives at yourstore.com/apps/cancel . Link it from your Shopify order confirmation, your FAQ, and your account page.

title: Reasons, questions and offers
text: Product groups, follow-up questions, and the offer each reason shows. Reasons are what customers pick when they cancel. Each reason can ask follow-up questions and show one offer. Product groups Different products get cancelled for different reasons. A snowboard might be cancelled because the customer doesn't have bindings yet, boots because they're worried about the fit. Product groups let each kind of product have its own list. Go to Reasons & offers and click Add product group . Choose which products belong to it by collection, product, or product tag. Add the reasons for that group. Groups are checked from the top. If a product fits two groups, the higher one wins. Everything else is always last and covers every product not in a group. There's no limit on how many groups you can have. If an order has items from two groups, the customer answers once per group, not once per item. Shared reasons Reasons like "Found a better price" or "Wrong shipping address" apply to everything. Set them up once under Shared reasons . They show after each group's own reasons, and you can turn one off for a specific group. Follow-up questions Questions open under a reason when the customer picks it: choose one, short text, long text, or a product picker. The answers show on each cancellation and in Overview, so you can see the real cause, like "is missing bindings". Offers Each reason can show one offer: Suggest products : add-ons that solve the problem. A product can show to everyone or only for certain answers. Discount : a code or a partial refund. Swap item : change the variant or product instead of cancelling. Shipping upgrade : a faster method at no cost. Fix address : edit the shipping address before it ships. Message only : a short note and a link. No offer : go straight to the cancel button. The customer can always cancel. Offers never hide the cancel button.

title: Cancellation rules
text: Decide which orders can be cancelled, and whether you approve them first. Rules run when the customer looks up their order, before any reasons or offers. They decide what happens: Auto-cancel : refunded and restocked right away. Needs approval : the order stays paused until you approve or decline it. Block : the customer sees your message instead, like "Your order is already being packed." How rules are checked From the top of the list; the first rule that matches decides. Drag the handle to change the order. The last rule, Everything else , covers every order the rules above didn't match. Orders that already shipped can never be cancelled in the portal. Conditions Every condition is picked from your store, not typed: order total, time since the order, time of day, customer tag, order tag, collection, product, product tag, payment method, and shipping country. Match all or any of them. Common setups Block cancels after your daily cutoff (for example after 2 p.m. for same-day shipping). Approve big orders yourself. Block wholesale customers or final sale items.

title: Managing cancellations
text: The cancellations list, approvals, and what you see on each one. Cancellations lists every request, with tabs for Needs approval , Saved , Cancelled and Blocked . Each cancellation Click a row to see: Items : which were cancelled, which were kept, and anything added from an offer. What the customer told you : the reason and answers per product group, the offer they saw, and whether they took it. Summary : refund, revenue saved, and which rule applied. History : every step with times, from the hold to the refund. Approvals When a rule says Needs approval , the order stays paused. Click Approve cancel to refund and restock, or Decline to keep the order and resume shipping. Vantly Cancellations doesn't send its own emails; Shopify's standard notifications (like order cancelled and refund) go out from your Shopify settings.

title: Overview and analytics
text: Revenue saved, save rate, and why customers cancel. Overview shows how your cancel portal is doing: Revenue saved : orders customers kept after seeing an offer. Save rate : the share of cancel requests that ended in a kept order. Why customers cancel : each reason, how often it was picked, and how often you saved it. What the answers say : follow-up answers for a reason, so you can spot the real cause. Offer performance : how often each offer was shown and accepted. Pick any date range, from Today to All time or your own dates, and compare with the previous period or the same period last year.

title: When is Vantly Cancellations available?
text: It's in development and coming soon to the Shopify App Store. Email support@vantlyapps.com to hear when it launches.

title: Can customers cancel only part of an order?
text: Yes. Every item starts selected, and customers untick what they want to keep. The refund covers only what they cancel, and the rest ships as planned.

title: Can a customer always cancel?
text: Yes, as long as your rules allow it. Offers never hide the cancel button.

title: Do customers have to give a reason?
text: Yes, one reason per product group they're cancelling. Follow-up questions are optional unless you make them required.

title: What stops my warehouse from shipping while the customer decides?
text: The order goes on a fulfillment hold as soon as the customer starts. It's released if they keep the order.

title: Can different products have different reasons?
text: Yes. Product groups give snowboards, boots, or any other kind of product their own reasons, questions and offers. There's no limit on groups.

title: What if the order has already shipped?
text: The portal won't cancel it. You can point customers to your return portal instead.

title: Does it work with Vantly Returns?
text: Yes. Both share your portal branding, and they're built to be used together.

title: Can I make the cancel portal match my store?
text: Yes. On the Cancel portal page, the Look tab sets your logo (and its position), colors, and font, and a Side by side or Classic layout, the same as Vantly Returns. The Text tab lets you change every piece of wording, grouped by step.

title: Do customers need an account?
text: No. They find their order with the order number and email.

title: Does Vantly send emails to my customers?
text: No. Shopify's own notifications (order cancelled, refund, payment link) go out from your Shopify settings.

title: How Vantly Discounts works
text: Discounts, cart groups and proposals, and how checkout picks the offer. Vantly Discounts lets one Shopify discount hold many offers. Instead of making a separate discount for "30% off boards" and "25% off bindings with a board", you make one discount with two proposals , built from reusable cart groups . The three parts Discount : how customers get it (a code or automatic), when it runs, who can use it, and what it combines with. Cart groups : named sets of products, like "Boards" or "Bindings". All is built in and holds every item. Proposals : "when the cart has this, discount those lines by this much". A proposal can take money off items, the order subtotal, or shipping. How checkout picks the offer Product proposals are checked from the top of the list; each item gets at most one, so the first proposal an item fits wins. For order and shipping proposals, the first one that qualifies wins. Drag ⋮⋮ to change the order, and switch a proposal off without deleting it. The discount is worked out inside Shopify's checkout, so it's fast and keeps working even if Vantly is briefly unavailable. Make your first discount Click Create discount . Everything is on one page: give it a name, pick Discount code or Automatic , and set the schedule and conditions on the right. Click Add cart group for the products you want to discount. Groups and proposals open in a pop-up. Add proposals (for example Add product proposal ) that say what each group gets: an amount, a percentage, or a fixed price. Summary describes each one in a plain sentence. Click Create discount at the top to save it to Shopify. Until then, nothing is saved. Turn on Test mode , add products to your cart as a customer tagged test , and check the price. The discount also shows in Shopify's own discount list, and opening it there brings you back to Vantly's editor.

title: Cart groups
text: Group products by collection, tag, metafield or price, and reuse them. A cart group is a named set of products that proposals check and discount, like "Boards" or "Bindings". Only you see the name. What can put an item in a group Products (pick as many as you like), Collection , or Product tag (is or is not). Product metafield equals or doesn't equal a value (the product's metafield; variant metafields aren't checked). Line attribute equals or doesn't equal a value. Line quantity or Item price is at least an amount. Purchase type : one-time or subscription. Compare-at price : set (already on sale) or none (not already on sale). Order matters Choose whether an item joins when it fits All conditions or Any condition . Groups are checked from the top. An item joins only the first group it fits, unless you turn on An item can join every group it fits . All always holds every item in the cart. Limits One discount can use up to 100 different collections and 100 different product tags across its groups, but each one you check lowers the biggest cart the discount works on (see A discount isn't applying ). Groups that use a metafield or line attribute need its key under Advanced on the discount; Shopify allows one of each per discount.

title: Proposals
text: When the cart has…, discount these lines…, by: amount, percentage or fixed price. A proposal is one offer inside a discount. It has two parts. 1. When the cart has The conditions the cart must meet. Pick a Measure (Quantity, Total, Unique products, Unique variants, or Unique groups), at least or at most, an amount, and the group to count In group . Add more with And another condition . With no conditions, it applies to every cart. 2. Discount these items (Product proposals only.) Pick the group to discount, or All (every item) , and How many : leave it at All, or enter a number to discount only the cheapest ones. Add another group discounts items in more groups. 3. By Pick a Discount type : Amount : money off each item, for example $50 off. Percentage : percent off each item, for example 25% off. Fixed price : the item sells for a set price, for example $149. On an order proposal, Amount and Percentage come off the order subtotal (Fixed price isn't offered). On a shipping proposal, Amount comes off each shipping option, Percentage off shipping (100% makes it free), and Fixed price sets what shipping costs, for example $4.99. Turn on Apply to compare-at price to take the discount off the higher compare-at price instead of today's price (never more than today's price). Use up the matched items With Use up the matched items on, items counted toward this proposal can't count toward later ones, and with a number in How many, the offer repeats for every full set in the cart (for example, buy 2 boards and get 1 binding free, for each set). Currency A proposal works in All currencies by default (amounts are converted from your store currency), or pick one currency so it only applies to carts in that currency.

title: Codes, limits and combining
text: Codes vs automatic, usage limits, schedules, and stacking with other discounts. How customers get it Choose Discount code (customers enter it; codes aren't case-sensitive and have no spaces) or Automatic (applies by itself at checkout). Who, how often, and with what Limit total uses and One use per customer . Combines with : product, order, and shipping discounts. Subscriptions : all recurring payments, or the first payment only. Conditions Turn on Only some currencies , Only some countries , or Only customers with tags (type the tags, separated by commas) to limit the whole discount, Require a cart attribute , and choose Include B2B customers . Test mode gives it only to customers tagged test . Schedule Set when it starts and, optionally, when it ends. Times are in your store's time zone. The list shows each discount as Active, Scheduled, Expired, Draft, or Needs attention.

title: A discount isn't applying
text: Test mode, conditions, priority, and what "Needs attention" means. Work through these in order. 1. Is it live? A Draft isn't in checkout yet; the discount page lists what's missing (for example, it needs at least one proposal). Scheduled hasn't started; Expired has ended. 2. Is Test mode on? With Test mode on, only customers tagged test get the discount. 3. Do the conditions fit? Check customer tags, countries, currencies, B2B, and any required cart attribute. Then check the proposal's "When the cart has" conditions against the cart. 4. Is another proposal winning? Each item gets at most one product proposal: the first one it fits. Move the one you expect higher, or check whether the item is in the group you think (it joins only the first group it fits unless that's turned off). 5. Does it combine? If the cart already has another discount, check Combines with on both. What "Needs attention" means Vantly couldn't update the discount in Shopify, for example because a group was deleted, a metafield key is missing, it uses more than 100 collections or tags, it's too big for Shopify (see the size meter under Summary ), or you're on the Free plan and another discount is already on. Shopify keeps using the last version that worked until you fix it. The discount page says what's wrong.

title: When is Vantly Discounts available?
text: It's in development and coming soon to the Shopify App Store. Email support@vantlyapps.com to hear when it launches.

title: Can one discount have several offers?
text: Yes. That's the point: one discount holds many proposals, checked from the top, for products, the order, and shipping.

title: Can an item get two proposals?
text: No. Each item gets at most one product proposal: the first one it fits.

title: Can I discount only the cheapest items?
text: Yes. In the proposal, under Discount these items, set How many to a number and the cheapest ones are discounted.

title: Does it work with codes and automatic discounts?
text: Yes, either one. You can switch later.

title: Can I test a discount before customers see it?
text: Yes. Turn on Test mode and only customers tagged test get it.

title: Does it stack with my other discounts?
text: Only if you allow it under Combines with, on this discount and the other one.

title: Does it work with subscriptions?
text: Yes. Choose all recurring payments or the first payment only.

title: How do I set up buy one, get one free?
text: Make a cart group for the product. Add a product proposal: under When the cart has, Quantity at least 1 in that group; under Discount these items, How many 1 in the same group; Percentage 100; and turn on Use up the matched items. It repeats for each pair: 2 in the cart gets 1 free, 4 gets 2 free.

title: How do I set up buy 3, get 1 at 50% off?
text: Same as buy one, get one: Quantity at least 3 in the group, How many 1 in the same group, Percentage 50, and Use up the matched items on. 4 in the cart gets 1 at half price, 8 gets 2. The cheapest one is the discounted one.

title: Is there a limit on how big a discount can be?
text: Yes, Shopify's. Shopify passes at most 10,000 bytes of settings per discount to checkout: about 590 hand-picked products, or about 45 proposals. The Discount size meter under Summary shows how full it is, and warns when it gets close. If it gets too big, Vantly won't send it to Shopify; use collections or tags instead of long product lists, or split it into two discounts.

title: Why does Summary say the discount works on carts up to a number of items?
text: Every collection and tag a discount checks is sent along with every item in the cart, and Shopify caps how much it sends. Checking many collections or tags lowers the biggest cart the discount still works on. Check fewer collections or tags, or combine them into one.

title: What does the Free plan include?
text: Every feature, with one discount turned on at a time (live or scheduled). A discount you add while one is already on is saved but stays off, marked Needs attention, until you upgrade or end the other one. Discounts that are already on keep working.

title: How do I upgrade to Pro?
text: Open Settings > Plan and billing and click Upgrade to Pro. Shopify shows its plan page; Pro starts with a 14-day free trial and is billed through your Shopify invoice. Pro runs as many discounts as you like.

title: Does it slow down checkout?
text: No. The discount runs inside Shopify's checkout as a Shopify Function; it never waits on Vantly's servers.
